claims.text: Binance froze around half of the stolen funds after $6.3 billion was accessed in a cyber heist.
Binance secured $3 billion of its stolen digital assets, while remaining funds were held by unidentified hackers.
Analytics firms linked the Binance hack to a North Korean hacking unit.
The Binance cyber heist eclipsed a $1.5 billion hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025.
The US Secret Service stated it was working around the clock to identify, freeze, trace, and recover stolen Binance funds.
Binance co-CEO Richard Teng stated that hackers used a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and traces as they went.
Binance set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the stolen assets.
The price of Bitcoin fell 5% to $76,800 in Friday afternoon trading in New York following news of the Binance hack.
Binance was founded in China in 2017 and is estimated to have over 300 million registered users worldwide.
Experts, including TRM Labs, attributed the $6.3 billion Binance cryptocurrency theft to TraderTraitor, an elite North Korean hacking unit also known as the Lazarus Group.
A UN panel of experts reported in spring 2024 that it was reviewing 58 suspected North Korean cyber-attacks on cryptocurrency companies between 2017 and 2023 worth $3 billion.
Cryptocurrency theft is estimated to generate half of North Korea's foreign currency income.
In February 2016, North Korean hackers attempted to illicitly move $951 million from Bangladesh Bank's account at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, ultimately stealing $81 million.
Blockchain intelligence firm TRM reported that an attacker moved approximately $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, mostly within 20 minutes.
Chainalysis co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin stated on X that the Binance hack was likely done by the DPRK group TraderTraitor.
Former Binance CEO Changpeng Zhao was pardoned by US President Donald Trump in 2025 after pleading guilty in 2023 to failing to prevent money laundering on the platform.
NyxLab CEO Kok Tin Gan stated the attack appeared to involve one signature granting a never-expiring, full-access token to a Binance hot wallet.
Benjamin Netanyahu accused Palestinian Israeli parties of stealing the Israeli election and accepting funding from Qatar.
Israel's Electoral Commission found no evidence of fraud regarding Palestinian Israeli parties, and Qatar denied involvement.
Israeli security agency Shin Bet investigated suspicions regarding whether Arab-led parties received illegal foreign funding from Qatar and Turkey.
The Arab party lists The Joint List and Ra'am won a record 19 seats in the 120-seat Knesset following high turnout among Arab voters.
Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats in the Israeli parliamentary election, while Gadi Eisenkot's rival bloc secured 48 seats.
Acting Central Elections Committee Director General Dean Livne stated there was no basis for allegations of systematic violations of election integrity.
Arab Israelis make up approximately one-fifth of Israel's population.
German Foreign Ministry spokesperson Martin Giese stated Germany will do everything possible to work well with any future Israeli government.
German Development Minister Reem Alabali Radovan called for an immediate stop to radical Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank and East Jerusalem.
Around 3,000 Palestinians were driven from their homes during a major Israeli military operation near Hebron following the reported killing of two Israeli soldiers.
Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party won 27 seats, remaining the largest party in the Knesset, but his right-wing coalition won 53 seats, short of the 61 needed for a majority.
In Israel, a candidate given the mandate to form a government has 28 days to secure support from at least 61 lawmakers, with a possible extension of up to 14 days.
US President Donald Trump endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu prior to the Israeli election.
Hundreds of residents were evacuated from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky during a four-hour window as part of a humanitarian ceasefire.
The localized humanitarian ceasefire in Oleshky was brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump.
Ukrainian negotiator David Arakhamia stated that evacuated residents of Oleshky traveled to Anapa in Russia, from where they would fly to Belarus and travel by bus to Ukraine.
Russia's human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova stated that 25 buses and nine ambulances were deployed for the Oleshky evacuations.
The population of Oleshky declined from a pre-war total of 24,000 to approximately 2,000.
A Russian drone strike on a train station in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro killed at least 13 people on Thursday.
The localized ceasefire allowed roads leading out of Oleshky to be de-mined to make evacuations possible.
The Kremlin described the Oleshky ceasefire as a special case that was difficult to extrapolate to broader peace negotiations.
Oleshky was captured by Russian forces in February 2022 and suffered severe flooding following the destruction of the Kakhovka dam in June 2023.
Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets stated this was the first time since 2022 that a ceasefire across such an extensive frontline stretch was maintained for a significant duration.
Polish police entered the Constitutional Tribunal premises in Warsaw after demonstrators gathered outside and threw objects at officers.
Constitutional Tribunal head Bogdan Swieczkowski was suspended after using his authority to block judges elected by the parliamentary majority from performing court duties.
Justice Minister Waldemar Zurek requested that legal immunity be lifted for Bogdan Swieczkowski and his deputy so they could face criminal charges.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk stated on X that restoring the rule of law after years of PiS lawlessness is a difficult, sometimes painful process requiring decisive action.
Polish President Karol Nawrocki turned his plane around while en route to Senegal, stating the president must be in Poland during the court crisis.
Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska was placed in charge of the Constitutional Tribunal following Swieczkowski's suspension.
The Constitutional Court published a statement on social media calling the actions against its top judges a coup d'etat and insisting they remain legally appointed.
President Karol Nawrocki has refused to swear in five Constitutional Court judges elected by parliament since March.
The Venice Commission advised President Nawrocki earlier in October to swear in the parliament-elected judges to allow them to sit on the bench.
Supporters of the opposition Law and Justice party gathered outside the Constitutional Tribunal chanting Tusk traitor and praying.
Independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta announced its closure after being evicted from its office of 30 years and blocked from receiving reader donations.
Novaya Gazeta co-founder Dmitry Muratov won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2021 and was designated a foreign agent by Russian authorities in 2023.
Six Novaya Gazeta journalists have been killed over the years, including Anna Politkovskaya who was shot dead in October 2006.
Novaya Gazeta investigative journalist Oleg Roldugin was arrested earlier in 2026 and charged with unlawful access to computerized information.
Novaya Gazeta editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov was questioned by police and had his home searched in connection with Roldugin's case.
Editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov wrote on Novaya Gazeta's website that the newspaper found itself in a kill zone after nearly five years of working while encircled by security services.
Following Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, Novaya Gazeta published blank white spaces in print to indicate censored text.
Dmitry Muratov was doused with red paint while on a train in April 2022, causing damage to his eyesight.
Exiled Novaya Gazeta journalists set up Novaya Gazeta Europe, while Muratov's team in Russia printed magazines with runs of 999 copies to bypass official licensing requirements.
Landlords informed Novaya Gazeta staff that they must vacate their central Moscow office newsroom by November 9.
